Description:
  Rewrite files to the line endings .gitattributes declares for them, read through 'git check-attr'. The policy is never restated here, so one statement of it governs both what git stores and what this writes. A file declared text=auto that git's own detection calls binary - a NUL anywhere, a carriage return no line feed follows, or more than one control byte for every 128 that print - is left as git leaves it; one declared text, or given an eol alone, is rewritten whatever it holds, as git converts it.

Usage:
  dssharness fix-line-endings [options]

Options:
  --all                        Cover every file git tracks.
  --changed                    Cover the working set: what is staged, and what is changed and not staged.
  --check                      Refuse instead of rewriting, and list what does not match. Nothing is written.
  --json                       Write what was covered and what changed as JSON.
  -v, --verbose                Show detailed progress and child process output.
  -C, --directory <directory>  Directory to operate in (default: current directory).

  Put each host's copy of this repository in step with this tree: files whose content changed are written, files the source no longer has are deleted, and the copy is verified afterwards. The tree is read once for every host; a file that changes before it is carried fails the sync.

Usage:
  dssharness sync [options]

Options:
  --legs <legs>                Only the hosts these legs or leg sets run on: --legs a,b or --legs a b. Without it, every host a declared leg needs.
  --dry-run                    List what would be written and deleted, change nothing, and exit as the sync would: 13 where it would refuse - a directory it did not make, without --adopt; more deleted than sync.maxDeleteFraction allows; a worktree's copy another worktree of the same name holds.
  --adopt <adopt>              Take over these hosts' copies although the harness did not create them: --adopt vps or --adopt vps "wsl Ubuntu". Otherwise refused. What it would cost is reported either way.
  --pull <pull>                Bring these paths back from each host's copy instead of syncing to it, verified on arrival: each a file, or with a '/' at its end a directory, whose every file comes back, each named.
  --artifact <artifact>        Carry one run's kept artifacts to each host instead of syncing the tree: --artifact 20260917-100000-0a1b2c3d. What a step kept is what a later step on another host reads.
  -v, --verbose                Show detailed progress and child process output.
